goal: Boot the editor UI immediately, then load runtime assets and scene content asynchronously without violating the current executor contract: only one owner thread may call enqueue, flush, or sync. The design must remove startup blocking, keep ownership explicit, and avoid introducing a generic async framework.
confirmed_assumptions: The single legal executor owner is the current main/game thread.
Worker threads are allowed to call atomic RHI creation APIs and record CommandList instances, but they still must not call executor enqueue, flush, or sync entrypoints.

startup_blockers.detail: Engine::Run() currently calls RuntimeAssets::WaitUntilReady() and SubmitPendingUploads() before entering the main render loop, which blocks editor UI bootstrap.
Renderer constructor still calls scene.LoadSceneFromFile(...) synchronously before the renderer can show any loading UI.

threading_risks.detail: GpuScene comments explicitly state that RHI is not thread-safe and application code must guarantee ownership. This checkpoint therefore must lock a narrower rule: atomic resource creation and command recording are allowed on worker threads, but executor progression remains single-owner on the main thread.

RuntimeAssets already uses a worker task and records upload commands there. The checkpoint should keep this direction and make the ownership rule explicit instead of reverting back to CPU-only workers.

readiness_model_gap.detail: Scene async API still builds LogicalScene, CpuScene, and GpuScene in one worker path. That mixes pure CPU loading with potential GPU-side ownership.

hard_constraints.title: Single-thread executor ownership
hard_constraints.detail: Exactly one owner thread may call RHIExecutor enqueue, flush, or sync entrypoints. This checkpoint assumes the owner is the same main/game thread that drives the editor UI loop.

hard_constraints.title: Worker-side RHI is limited to atomic creation and recording
hard_constraints.detail: Worker threads may create resources and record CommandList instances, but they must not advance executor state or publish GPU readiness directly.

hard_constraints.title: UI must not wait for asset or scene readiness
hard_constraints.detail: Window creation, editor shell UI, and renderer bootstrap must complete before runtime asset uploads or scene GPU initialization finish.

hard_constraints.title: No generic async transport layer
hard_constraints.detail: Do not introduce a generic pipe, job bus, or framework-level async abstraction. Use narrow payload types dedicated to asset bootstrap and scene bootstrap only.

hard_constraints.title: Latest-only path
hard_constraints.detail: Do not keep both blocking startup and async startup paths alive as equal first-class flows. After migration, startup should use the async bootstrap path by default.

checkpoint.title: Split startup into async CPU loading and main-thread GPU adoption
checkpoint.problem: The engine currently blocks before the first visible frame. At the same time, current scene and asset loading code is not cleanly separated between CPU-only work and executor-owned GPU work, so simply moving all loading to worker threads would violate current ownership assumptions.
checkpoint.decision: Use a two-phase bootstrap model. Worker threads perform file IO, parsing, decoding, atomic RHI resource creation, and command-list recording. The main UI thread pumps ready payloads once per frame, submits those pre-recorded command lists, and is the only thread allowed to advance executor state.
target_flow: 1. Engine::Init() creates RenderDevice, WindowContext, and editor config as today, then starts async bootstrap jobs for runtime assets and scene CPU loading without waiting for them.
2. Engine::Run() enters the editor loop immediately. The renderer is created in a loading-capable state and must tolerate scene.IsReady() == false and runtime_assets.IsReady() == false.
3. Each frame, before render submission, the main thread calls one narrow bootstrap pump that checks whether asset or scene CPU payloads are ready.
4. When an asset payload is ready, the main thread adopts its pre-recorded upload command lists and submits them through the executor owner thread only.
5. When a scene payload is ready, the main thread adopts its pre-recorded GpuScene initialization command lists and submits them through the same executor owner thread only.
6. Once the corresponding GPU work has been submitted and any required completion fence is observed, the bootstrap state publishes RuntimeAssets and Scene readiness to the renderer.

worker_thread_allowed: GpuScene construction under the confirmed worker-side atomic RHI rule
CommandList recording and upload/init command assembly
CPU-side metadata preparation for later main-thread publication
main_thread_only: Any bootstrap state publication that exposes GPU-backed scene/assets to the renderer
Merging and draining multiple pending async payloads into one owner-thread submission point

required_design_changes.change: Remove the blocking WaitUntilReady() call from the startup path. Replace it with per-frame pumping of bootstrap payloads inside the main loop.
Renderer constructor must stop synchronously loading the scene. It should either request async scene loading itself or receive a Scene object that is already in 'loading' state.
Keep RuntimeAssets as an async recorded-submit producer. Tighten it so the worker only records payloads and the main thread only submits and publishes readiness.
Split Scene loading into async payload production and main-thread submission/publication. Worker path may construct GpuScene and record its initialization command lists, but must not submit them.
Make GpuScene an async-recordable producer that can be built off-thread under the confirmed atomic RHI rule, while keeping final executor progression on the main thread only.

recommended_payloads.name: AsyncAssetRecordedPayload
recommended_payloads.purpose: Carries pre-recorded upload command lists plus any post-submit CPU cleanup callbacks and readiness publication data for RuntimeAssets.

recommended_payloads.name: AsyncSceneRecordedPayload
recommended_payloads.purpose: Carries a ready LogicalScene, derived CpuScene, constructed GpuScene state, and pre-recorded initialization command lists for owner-thread submission.

ui_behavior: The first visible frames should render editor shell UI plus a loading state, not stall before window interaction is possible.
Renderer code paths that already guard on scene.IsReady() and runtime_assets.IsReady() should become the normal bootstrap behavior rather than an exceptional path.
Loading progress may remain coarse initially. Exact percentage progress is not required for this checkpoint.
non_goals: No background executor submission thread separate from the UI owner thread.
No automatic cross-submit resource-state inference added to make async payloads work.
No compatibility mode that preserves the old blocking startup path as a long-term option.
acceptance_criteria: Editor window and base UI can appear before runtime assets and scene are fully ready.
Only one thread performs executor enqueue/flush/sync calls during bootstrap and steady-state runtime.
RuntimeAssets and Scene each expose a non-blocking 'pump/adopt' step callable from the main loop.
Scene async loading may construct GpuScene on a worker thread, but it no longer submits GPU work there.
Renderer startup no longer blocks on RuntimeAssets::WaitUntilReady() or synchronous scene loading.

validation_plan: When implementation starts, validate only with existing scripts: testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1 first, then testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1.
This design checkpoint itself is documentation-only and does not require a build.
